Interesting! In the initial state, the bar had:
- b (8 pixels) at (19, 39) - 4x2 shape
- S (8 pixels) at (19, 41) - 4x2 shape
But now the bar shows:
- g (88 pixels) at (19, 17) - a long gray bar
- The small pair (b, S) is at the far right
So the initial bar had b and S segments that are now part of a gray bar! The b and S segments on the bar have been absorbed into the gray bar, and only the small movable pair remains.
Wait, actually looking more carefully:
- Initial: b (8 pixels) at (19, 39) and S (8 pixels) at (19, 41) - these are the movable pair segments
- Current: g (88 pixels) at (19, 17) - this is the gray bar track
So the initial bar had the pair at positions (19, 39) and (19, 41), and the gray bar extends from (19, 17) to (20, 40) or so. The pair moves along this gray track.
But I notice something important: in the initial state, the bar had TWO separate nodes for b and S (8 pixels each), but now the pair is at the far right and the bar is just gray. The pair's colors (b, S) are preserved as it moves.
OK let me think about this completely differently. I've spent 47 actions and haven't solved the level. Let me look at what I haven't tried:
1. I haven't tried clicking on the gray squares in the right grid
2. I haven't tried clicking on the center of the right grid
3. I haven't tried moving the pair to specific positions and then pressing UP/DOWN
4. I haven't tried clicking on the pair itself
Wait, actually, I just realized something. The initial right grid had white (W) squares at the cross positions. When I click on a white square, it turns green (N). When I click on a gray square, it also turns green. So clicking always paints green.
But what if I need to click on the gray squares (not the white ones) to complete the pattern? The initial pattern was:
Row 1: g W g
Row 2: W g W
Row 3: g W g
If the goal is to paint the gray squares green (leaving white squares as-is), then the target would be:
Row 1: N W N
Row 2: W N W
Row 3: N W N
But I've already painted everything green, so I need to reset first.
Let me try: reset the right grid by clicking the left grid, then paint only the gray squares (corners and center).
